answer.justification: The recurrent laryngeal nerve runs close to the inferior thyroid artery near the thyroid pole. Ligation of the inferior thyroid artery near the pole can injure this nerve, and unilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve injury typically causes hoarseness. External laryngeal nerve injury is more associated with superior thyroid artery ligation and voice fatigue/pitch change, while laryngeal edema would present earlier with stridor.
